findings.summary: A repeated index in subset= (or a repeated assumption in Solver.solve) raises IndexError, and the same extractor then returns a satisfiable set that verify() endorses
mus.py says deletion makes exactly |M| calls after the core; it makes |core|, which differs when the core is not minimal
cdclkit mus --method core --verify exits 1 and prints no clauses on a correct but non-minimal core; consistent with its help text

observations: Indices count CNF.clauses, so a tautology in the input, which CNF.add documents dropping, shifts them against the file's own clause numbering. The CLI prints each clause's body, and the harness checks the body against the index.
not_checked: negative and out-of-range indices in subset= and verify(): undocumented
MUSExtractor constructed on a CNF whose nvars was lowered by hand or whose .clauses was assigned directly: selector variables would collide; outside CNF's normalising interface
a CNF mutated after the extractor was built
the native engine: mus uses the Python Solver only, there is no native MUS path
formulas past the hard tier's 60 variables, and any claim about call counts (QuickXplain's O(|M| log(|F|/|M|))) beyond verify's cost and deletion's
minimum (smallest) MUS: documented as not attempted
Solver Config variations: MUSExtractor exposes no config parameter
